pr_title: WebGPURenderer: Support rotation of env maps.
pr_body:
Fixed #30523.

**Description**

The PR adds support for `Scene.environmentRotation` and `material.envMapRotation`. 

@sunag An open issue is a circular dependency that was the main reason why I not implemented this feature straight away with #29762:
```
src/nodes/accessors/MaterialNode.js -> src/nodes/accessors/ReferenceNode.js -> src/nodes/accessors/CubeTextureNode.js -> src/nodes/accessors/MaterialNode.js
```
Do you have an idea how to refactor the code so the circular dependency disappears?

issue_context.title: WebGPU & TSL envMapRotation
issue_context.body:
### Description

As far as I can tell, there is no `scene.environmentRotation` being applied in `WebGPURenderer` or TSL.
Same goes for `material.envMapRotation`. 
However, there is a reference to it in the TSL Specification, at `.envNode`: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/wiki/Three.js-Shading-Language#lighting.

### Solution

Implement `scene.environmentRotation` and `material.envMapRotation`.

### Alternatives

Add an `.envMapRotation` node to TSL, or a rotation parameter to `.envNode`?

### Additional context

Would be happy to be proven wrong on this!
On a related topic, is there a roadmap on which features are implemented or not in `WebGPURenderer` and TSL?
Thanks!
comments: Rotating environment maps isn't supported yet. Just `Scene.backgroundRotation`, see #29762.

review_comments: When adding `materialEnvRotation` to `MaterialNode`, I've fixed this TODO and also implemented `materialEnvIntensity`.
I moved to `Material Properties`. If we can use `uniform()` with `onRender Update()` it will be better than using `references()`.
I had to change the update scope from `render` to `object` otherwise different intensity values in different materials were not honored correctly. Same for rotation and refraction ratio.
